## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Migration 3 must back up `users` before it drops `legacy_email`: as written it deletes that column's data with no way to restore it, unlike the other two destructive migrations.

## Changes
The pull request adds migrations 3 and 4, which drop `users.legacy_email` and `orders.coupon_code`. It also adds one test that runs all four migrations and checks that both columns are gone and that the `orders` backup exists.

## Critical
- migrations/m0003_drop_legacy_email.py:7 — correctness — Back up users before dropping legacy_email — On any database with populated `users.legacy_email`, `upgrade` drops the column without calling `backup_table`, so no `users_backup_3` table exists. `migrations/safety.py:3-5` states that each destructive migration first calls `backup_table`. — Running migration 3 permanently deletes every stored legacy email, because rolling back the deploy cannot restore a dropped column. — Fix: Call `backup_table(conn, "users", VERSION)` first, as `migrations/m0002_drop_nickname.py:7` does, and extend `test_drop_retired_columns` with a populated `users` row.
